text: Unlike most RPGs, in BG3, poison is
trash. There's hardly any poison spells
in the game, and over 190 unique enemies
are completely immune. For comparison,
fire's got 37. You're better off unarmed
than using toxic magic. So, can you beat
Balders's Gate 3 using only poison
damage? Our hero today is Ivy, a green
dragon born sorcerer. Believe it or not,
a level one sorcerer already has more
than half of all poison spells available
in the game. While poisonless Lzelle
watches, let's quickly go over them.
chromatic orb poison, poison spray, ray
of sickness, and our lizard racial
poison breath. Thankfully, the nautaloid
is the tutorialist of tutorial zones
where even having no damage at all would
not be an issue. As we arrive on the
beach to begin act one, I'll explain the
should be obvious rule. All damage my
characters deal must be poison. [music]
So, no damage riders, no throwing things
which would deal bludgeoning, just
poison from this party. With even Gail's
eventual necrotic corpse being a risk I
cannot take. From what I can tell, the
poison spray cantrip is our number one
tool, and its damage is actually okay.
The range and hit chance, however, are
kind of crap. With this first victory
under our belt, we adorn some green
threads. And because we're a magic focus
group, the magical Disney swamp is our
first destination. After greeting Shrek
here, things are going to get weird. As
Shadow Heart lifts up a Star by
canceling throw within one frame of
starting it, she's next poisoned by her
own allies. The fresh corpse stuffed
into a box to be flung into the act one
asylum. Saving and reloading the game
from here causes Aarian to pop out of
the box. While there's a lot of fun
characters in here, like these five
Raphaels, four emperors, and a werewolf,
the dude we're after is Kazador.
Spoiler, this dude's a vampire, and
using a strength elixir, we can kidnap
him out of the asylum to the beach where
the full concentrated power of the sun
burns him alive. The sun is not in my
party, and if this loophole bothers you,
dislike the video now because the Kather
Strat is going to give you an aneurysm.
Kazador can't actually die in act one as
he is flagged as immortal. But when he
drops to low health points, he will
strategically unequip his own staff. And
by using sanctuary, we can keep
attempting to pick his pockets, flee
through the door on a fail until
eventually his staff is my staff. Having
an act three weapon at level three is
already pretty cool, but why not make it
four? Using the invoke duplicity item
duke trick, I took four rings and four
staffs off of fake shadow heart to get
this poison run started, right? Had this
run been any damage type or green only,
this staff would be insane as woe grants
you a 64 damage blight spell, but
because blight is not poison, woe is
basically just 5% spell hit chance and
healing for 1d4 whenever I attack. Still
pretty decent, certainly not
gamebreaking. Freeing withers here would
have been nice, but nearly all undead in
the game are immune to my attacks.
Without a viable way to kill, these were
instead forced to sneak into the goblin
camp, unlocking withers in a less
satisfying way, but still becoming a
full sorcerer team. To give myself a
little challenge, I tried out these
powers on some of the most
poisonresistant enemies of act one. The
spiders were pretty tough, but really
not as bad as I'd expected. The spider
matriarch, however, is fully immune to
poison. Extra sad because she has one of
the only unique poison specific
equipment items in the game. Rip that
dream. On the plus side, I discovered
poisoning a broomer barrel will heal me,
and painting the battlefield in a color
other than red is oddly satisfying. Some
rooftop combat got me to level four, and
I was excited to pick up the elemental
adept poison feet until realizing that
doesn't exist. Yeah, okay, I get it.
Maybe poison isn't an element, but what
scientist out there decided acid is?
Well, that would have been nice. Act
one's combat probably isn't the hard
part of this challenge. Ignore the fact
that it looks like an owl bear's kicking
our asses because I can assure you it is
on purpose. I just wanted to collect the
corpses of these absolutists. You know,
normal player behavior. From a distance,
I cast Ray of Sickness on the goblin's
booze tub. Despite being clearly caught
in the act by an ogre, I guess he forgot
to tell the others cuz they drank up and
died before participating in a poison
pool party. The rest of the goblins will
be facing a very different fate. As I
alerted Menthora of the location of the
innocents waiting to be slaughtered in a
shocking twist, Zevllor is betrayed, but
in reverse, Uno, screw you. This is my
story move. I'm still siding with him
without his consent. Aarian on the side
snuck into combat, kidnapping Zevllor,
holding him hostage, ensuring combat
with these now Green Goblin allies will
not end until he is released from the
pocket realms. Keeping Zebl safe, I
spent 47 minutes spraying poison into
the eyes of my ever patient allies,
successfully double betraying them. I'd
always knew it was practically
impossible to lose here. I mean, it's
like 25 soldiers versus three and a half
refugees. But only when Menthara stood
alone against my pathetic 11% hit chance
did I learn it's literally impossible.
She dropped to zero HP showcasing
immortality. It's not often Lyion pulls
that [ __ ] I dropped Zevllure off in
the kid's hideout. And after combat
ended, I was able to kill her with
Zevllor still alive. Only time will tell
if any of that nonsense will affect the
story down the line. Returning to the
swamp and poisoning these red caps got
us to level 5, doubling the damage of
our poison spray cantrip to a
respectable 2d12. As annoying as it is,
these five levels have granted no new
poisonous spells to play with. Long way
to go still before that happens. Using
magic against the hag is ill- advised on
honor difficulty. Though with twin spell
ray of sickness, things went much better
than expected. Still couldn't save
Marina. Didn't even want to. She died
and the hag too faced a toxic end. Our
reward, nothing but a dead zombie
husband. Now that we've gathered his
corpse, we can enter the Underdark to
find more people to betray.
Interestingly enough, mushrooms are
immune to poison, but mushroom men
aren't even resistant. A situation we
take full advantage of, as this may be
the last time this happens for weeks.
The dwar by the beach are the beginning
of my pain. All dwarves are resistant to
poison damage, reducing their damage
taken from us by 50%. That does make
things take longer, but resistance is
kind of like paying taxes. It's
annoying. You can avoid it for a bit,
but in the end, you're going to get
[ __ ] and the government will take all
your YouTube money. No dwarves are left
alive as the rest of this location ain't
going to be any easier. Was somewhat
confused learning animated armor is not
poison immune. More confused seeing
magma methods are resistant and not at
all confused that myithil ore is not a
minable resource via our green magic.
Trying to poison the mimics in their
chest form proved impossible. But once
they opened their silly little mouths,
they happily choked on toxic goo.
Grimboards was just full of surprises.
them helping to reach level six is a
pretty big deal as the dragon born
sorcerer's ancestry bonus adds four
damage to all poison spells just in time
to take the elevator out of this zone
and begin act two the actual start of
the challenge Ivy's got no hope of
saving these Harpers as the shadows
asses are completely impenetrable by
poison along with a large amount of the
rest of act 2's asses there's no choice
for them but to die sneaking past the
shadows into Last Light in it's time to
meet the solution to my problems the
strange ox I was recently taught by some
smart individuals that for some reason
once you attack the strange aux all of
the Harpers and Flaming Fists in Last
Light in turn from yellow useless NPCs
to good guy green allies and they will
stay that way unless you betray them.
Green NPCs will help out when combat
starts nearby. Meaning on paper all you
need to do is lure any poison immune
creatures all the way to last light in
and they'll carry you to victory. While
it is a nice bonus, three Harpers died
during the first attempt meaning this
plan probably isn't that viable. plan to
use that tactic on the DRE caravan.
However, those weaklings kind of just
died during the kiting process before
even reaching town. Afraid Pixie means
moonrise is available. And within comes
likely the best poison item in the game.
Realistically, there's only like three
poison items in the game, so not much
competition. But this ring once per long
rest will make a target vulnerable to
poison as long as they aren't immune.
Absolutely insane versus bosses or ogres
or anything with a pulse. As the dark
urge these moonrise nullles can be
turned green by a dialogue choice. And
while their help isn't necessary versus
the weak little cultists, I figured they
should be able to handle these poison
immune ghouls. They could not. But by a
stroke of luck, one cultist threw a
costic bulb. And about 16 turns later,
Lzelle was shoved into that where a
ghoul mindlessly dipped his little toes
into acid, dying instantly without even
trying. My enemies solved my own problem
for me. An issue which can't be solved,
however, is the floaty moonrise
eyeballs. I'd sooner jump into a chasm
than waste another second on these
[ __ ] So, I did just that. [music]
After clearing out all other enemies,
the plan was to flee the Iron Hand
gnomes from prison. They turned green in
the process, helping me against the
scrying eyes, and all Woolburn has to do
is attack. Being a worthless piece of
trash, he refused to do anything at all.
I dropped a staff to boost his damage,
he equipped it, followed by doing
nothing. Even poisoned open a strength
elixir at his feet. Yet, bro continued
to do nothing. All you had to do was
swing at the eyeball, dude. His sudden
pacifism would cost him and his friends
their lives. Until now, every plan to
turn NPCs green to save my ass has been
extremely underwhelming. All it's taught
me is the only good ally is a dead one.
So, [ __ ] the Harpers. I'll be the toxic
teammate today and lure the plant boss
to them because I didn't know how to
make them green the last time I tried
this. Realistically, how many Harpers
could one boss kill anyways? If you
guess literally all of them, plus the
flaming fists and a random house cat,
then you're a smarter person than I.
This was an outcome past proxy never
expected. The main issue they ran into
is that the Harpers mostly use piercing
damage and this plant boss is fully
immune to that specifically. Rip Jahira
too. Well, with her death, there's no
more friends with lives to ruin. Our
party can enter the mausoleum to not do
the gauntlet of Char. For to begin any
of those trials, a party member would
have to slit their own wrist, which
makes them bleed outside the cutscene
and is self-inflicted non-poison damage.
Instead, we're grabbing a spear, which I
was kind of surprised was possible to
do, as these undead aren't poison
immune. Then sneaking up to poison
immune jurgger, we grab his little
elevator powering gem. Knock goes the
door and into the shadow fell we are.
It's been 12 years, but on this day, the
night song will not be speared in a
proxy video as poison immune unkillable
Balthazar is chosen as our ally. Forgot
this pisses off Shadow Heart, so she's
joining the betrayed allies list,
replaced by Sir Fuzzle Lump himself.
Back at the tower top, we sneak up to
Catholic's rooftop to report the Night
Song's capture as per the quest, only
for him to gaslight me. He explained,
"Belazar already told me to go kidnap
Isabelle." Had to double check the
dialogue logs because no, bro, that did
not happen. Clearly, Zarell being dead
while siding with Katherrick was not
play tested properly. With no plans to
help an abusive old man kidnap his own
daughter, I approach the altar, praying
to the absolute, becoming kidnapped
myself. Experiencing the pain of
betrayal I'd forced upon so many before.
We wake up to find Balthazar has us in
zombie prison hell. He's still not
killable. So using the sorcerer's subtle
metamagic power, we misty step to
invisible freedom. Walting into the
tadpole room to screw over yet another
ally, Gauntlet Ya. This time, no attempt
at aid is given in her struggle against
the mind flares. As is tradition, an RP
walk towards Kather's elevator plays
out, which can mean only one thing.
Another insanely stupid jank Katherric
strat is about to go down. Part of the
reason I sided with Balthazar [music]
this time was to avoid battling
Katherine on his rooftop. He is a 100%
poison damage immune mandatory boss,
which means the challenge effectively
ends with him. Alien can't solo him on
honor mode, and with no other living
allies in the colony, you're screwed.
It's impossible to beat BG3 using only
poison. However, I have brought a proxy
cheese fil box with me. The solution to
our problem, dead NPCs. Let's get these
corpses out on the floor and explain
Conormancy. [music] Back in the Hair, I
grabbed Connor's corpse and the
bitter divorce wand. This wand can
target Connor to revive him. However, if
you target another dead NPC as the
revived destination, it will revive both
Connor and that NPC. Normally kind of
useless as these revived NPCs break and
don't do anything. But as this spider
here was green to me when it died back
at the goblin gates, once revived, it
retains its allied status, killing
poison immune Connor for me. The past
toxic behavior of betraying all my
allies was all so that I could bring
them back in the greatest act of
necromancy known to mankind. Full
transparency, I didn't test this idea in
advance, and it was a lot more annoying
than I expected. For some reason, the
game needs to be saved and reloaded
every single time you revive Connor for
them to kill him. I mean, obviously,
this wasn't an intended mechanic in the
first place, so I can't be one to
complain. I guess that little [music]
annoyance meant it took several hours of
saving and reloading just to get all of
these guys alive. The next problem is
once alive, they only have 3 HP.
Throwing a health potion does
bludgeoning damage. That's not allowed.
But despite potions supposedly being
immune to poison, I discovered they
break on hit from any spell, including
poison spray. Overall, the necromancy
prep phase took far too long for me to
ever recommend anyone do this. But after
about 4 hours, Katherine, let me
introduce you to my tight crew. And to
start the encounter, we're going to use
some poison on Kendrick. The man may be
poison immune, but Kerazan's poison from
the undead nurse lady can be dropped at
his feet and poisoned open to perma stun
his human form. The ithids in the room
are the only targets I can hurt. So once
they're dead, it's all up to my
makeshift horde of 50-ish allied idiots.
I did help a bit by kidnapping
necromites out of Kather's honor mode
[ __ ] respawn aura. But all damage is
100% up to these clowns. Phase one went
to plan. Things tend to go well when
your enemy never has a turn. In fact,
the only one killing our team was Alien
with her driveby moon beam and radiant
splash attacks. Fist Jelar pushed him
into Merkel phase where poison damage
continues to do nothing. And now my
stuns too will no longer work. With no
more healing potions available, all I
can do is sit back and watch as the
Harper shockingly miss all of their
attacks. And Ailen repeatedly wrecks her
own allies. Each of Merkel's swings
would cleave six or seven dudes at a
time, making my brow sweat ever so
slightly. Many more long strings of low
or no damage by my useless friends
occurred, and as fresh necroines began
popping up, the butterflies in my
stomach grew. Somehow with each video,
the Merkel strat is taking exponentially
longer and getting more annoying. In a
surprise to all, the MVP award for the
best performance goes to Wuburn. While
in life, he was a useless little [ __ ] as
a zombie, he frequently manhandled two
necromites per turn. Impactful because
whenever Necromites popped up, everyone
else decides to stop hitting Merkel and
focus only them down. Despite my allies
best efforts, yeah, that's probably
their best. Merkel still got a heal off
then cleave six more dudes. Most allies
remained pumping less DPS than even
Scott's worst Warcraft [music] logs. And
as he neared singledigit health, I found
myself fist pumping for NPCs. With 5 HP,
who would get the final blow? The Night
Song. Surely the Night Song. No, of
course not. She's useless. Instead, it's
Harper Shenty who claims glory. Without
any non-poison damage from a controlled
character, Honor Merkel is slain. Harper
Shenti's reward is being the only NPC
allowed to leave the colony. The proxy
games are over and we can finally leave
this cursed land for good and get back
to using poison like the challenge was
meant to be. After being unable to
participate in battle for so long,
giving it back to the GIF in camp felt
cathartic. Poisoning them to death was
the joy I needed at this moment. After
ignoring the emperor's lies, act three
begins with that previous stun poison
being much more effective against Kather
than I ever dreamed of. On the GR, I
tested out the other poison elixirs the
world has to offer. And while I did
appreciate seeing the rainbow of poison
colors, they're all pretty trash. Near
their camp, I found a child's drawing
I'd not seen before. I believe that dude
on the right is Gortach. Both Beach Boy
factions were slaughtered as I no longer
need to collect the dead. And it was
here we finally reached level 9,
unlocking a new poison spell, probably
the best poison spell, cloud kill. Got
to say, it is great to finally have an
area of effect attack. The easiest way
to start act three as always is a trip
to sorcerer sundries. Can't kill heroic,
but his legendary staff is a free best
in slot. Kazador's mansion is next for
the insane XP with even the 28 health
point guys rewarding 400 each. Had to
pickpocket the ring off of the poison
immune skeleton. But seeing the XP re in
as creatures poured into a cloud kill
was well worth the trip. For funsies, I
snuck up on Kazador to return his staff
as I felt this bro deserved a fighting
chance against us. Though our poison
vulnerability ring let us rip him apart
in record speeds. Chatter teeth and the
zombies did near the game over us. Had
no choice but to flee. Aarium was going
to sneak back in solo to ascend or not.
Never saw this play out when a star ends
up there alone without Tav and he
decided to free all the vampires on his
own. I mean that was pretty wholesome of
him. There are a few more poison spells
available in the game and it's only in
this video that I'll get a chance to
talk about them. Two of them are
purchased off the mysticarion and
attached to a druid specific item.
Timisk spores and bibberbang spores both
usable only once per long rest. Surely
Timis spores being a guaranteed stun due
to all my spell DC items must make it
one overpowered effect in combat, right?
No, of course not. Because in Laren's
world, 8 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 1 equals 10,
which is less than 13. So, it fails to
land. Regardless of this item being
bugged, it's worth using just for its
haste scores alone, at least. There is
one final poison spell we're going to
get at level 11. So until then, we get
back to the main story. Thankfully,
poisoning the hanging corpse still
generates the blood necessary to open
the sewer door. And in Manslaughter
Chasm, I rushed in blindly to poison the
sewer scum. Then quickly realize this
red ghost is not killable. That's fine.
I'll use knock to get through the door.
Knock doesn't work either. I could just
reload and sneak through invisibly, but
it's here that I noticed that there's a
countdown timer on the lock. What
happens if you wait the full 99 turns
that it's blocked by ballist mischief?
Let's find out. And after waiting 594
seconds, the door pops open. Just like
that, we're off to Orin's Temple, where
for the first time in a year, I get to
actually play the game in a somewhat
normal fashion. Orin is not her usual
gigantic pain in the ass self. Cloudkill
chokes her channelers, and I can misty
step around the room having a gay old
time. The only slight hiccup was her
skeletons being unkillable, which
doesn't explain why my characters died.
That was just due to me playing poorly.
She fell and I made my embarrassing
escape from the skeletons. Next, getting
to see the Dark Urge cutscene still play
on our dead hero. Because I'm me and I
enjoy breaking things, I revived her
with Withers back in camp and totally
[music] broke the cut scene. Now I have
no idea what ending we'll get. The
butler is so broken he won't even
acknowledge our existence. Nabber
threatened us, so we [music] had no
choice but to defend ourselves from him,
granting one experience and level 11,
where I can finally switch to wizard and
unlock the last pure poison spell in the
game, Condra Elemental Water Merrmadon.
When these little water bros are
poisoned, their AoE heal will deal
poison damage instead of doing the heal.
And who better to use this power against
than Gortach? [music]
The Steel Watchers are another
non-killable target. So for this
handsome young man, I prepared a special
little something. After Starion starts
the encounter by reading Gortach's diary
here, he can travel to the second floor
where no NPC can figure out how to path
up here or hit you unless they walk
through the arcane gate. Steel watchers
are too large to enter the portal,
eliminating their problem entirely and
giving time for our elemental to munch
on a rotten bit of food, get poisoned,
and drop a massive AoE poison nuke in
the room for like eight damage or
something. I don't know. It was honestly
pretty underwhelming. Once Gortach alone
took the arcane gate, I canceled
concentration, giving me a 4v1 scenario.
He ended up trapped against the wall by
furniture, adding to his embarrassment.
As long as you don't stand exactly where
I stood with this little gnome dude,
nobody downstairs can hit you, and you
can just blast poison at his face all
day long. And by reading Gortach's diary
to start the encounter, it means that
the keep doesn't turn red like normal
when you talk to him, so you can just
flee the battle after. Revive your
allies and come back to loot the final
Netherstone. The jump scare of combat
immediately after the cutscene was a
good startle. How these three steel
watchers suddenly snuck up on me is a
mystery I'll never solve. The usual
morphic pool boat trip plays out. Brain
cats are poisoned. the emperor joined
and invisibly we skipped the courtyard
as all of these encounters have things I
can't kill. The actual Netherbrain
encounter itself was slightly more
annoying than usual due to the 7,000
counter spells that these dudes have.
Also because a sheep can't wield the
nether stones, but after much time and
many game overs, we made it inside. The
5% hit chance vulnerability was never
going to happen. Though even without it,
we just kind of started blasting. On
honor mode, you can't repeat the same
damage type two turns in a row. So our
first turn was completely wasted due to
stuns. But Aarian's haste spores enabled
us to pump it green regardless. The
brain was felled. And if you count all
of the jank at Kthrick, I beat
Boulders's gate three using only poison
damage. Without intending it, every one
of us got the bad endings we deserved
for our toxic behavior. Lazelle's killed
by her own queen. Aarian turned bald.
Our hero Ivy's driven mad by bald and
pissed herself. And another successful
challenge wraps up. If you enjoyed this
challenge run, consider leaving a like
on the video and then go check out the
companion cube challenge run here. As
always, huge thanks to my channel
members for your support. And until next
year, proxy out.
